chunks: Whoever bequeaths [with] a third has not left anything out.

key_terms.أَوْصَى: bequeathed — the act of making a wasiyyah (testamentary bequest), one of the key mechanisms in Islamic estate law
key_terms.الثُّلُثُ: the third — the maximum portion of an estate a Muslim may dispose of by bequest, as established in fiqh and derived from Prophetic hadith

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about bequeathing one third of one's estate in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms that bequeathing one third of one's estate is sufficient and complete — leaving nothing undone with respect to one's testamentary obligations. This hadith addresses a question in Islamic inheritance law: the permissible maximum for a bequest is one third of the estate, and using this maximum amount is a complete and praiseworthy act. The original audience — students of fiqh in Medina and Kufa — would have understood this as confirmation that the one-third limit established in Prophetic hadith and referenced in Quran is the full extent of rightful disposition, beyond which the rights of heirs begin.
